questions.question: What is the term for the ability of new software or hardware to work with older versions of software or hardware?
questions.explanation: Backward compatibility is defined as the ability of new software or hardware to work with older versions.

questions.question: According to the lesson, what is the primary purpose of a 'System Upgrade'?

options.A: To completely replace an old system with a new one
options.B: To enhance performance, add new features, or fix problems
options.C: To make different systems communicate with each other
options.D: To design independent parts for easy replacement

questions.explanation: A system upgrade is defined as a change or improvement made to a system to enhance its performance, add new features, or fix problems.

questions.question: What does 'Modularity' mean in the context of system design?

options.A: The ability of different systems to work together seamlessly
options.B: Designing a system with independent parts that can be easily replaced or upgraded
options.C: The process of finding the best possible solution under constraints
options.D: Permanent software programmed into read-only memory

questions.explanation: Modularity is defined as designing a system with independent parts (modules) that can be easily replaced or upgraded without affecting the entire system.

questions.question: Why is designing for system upgrades important for a product's 'Sustainability'?

options.A: It allows the product to be completely redesigned every few years
options.B: It ensures the product can continue functioning and serving its purpose over a long period
options.C: It makes the product cheaper to produce initially
options.D: It prevents any future changes or improvements from being made

questions.explanation: Upgrades keep systems fresh and useful for longer, ensuring a product's ability to continue functioning and serving its purpose over a long period, which is the definition of sustainability.

questions.question: The lesson uses the analogy of upgrading kitchen appliances or adding solar panels to a house. What does this analogy primarily illustrate about system upgrades?

options.A: That all upgrades require tearing down the entire structure
options.B: That the main structure of a system should be designed to accommodate future improvements
options.C: That houses are more complex than most technological systems
options.D: That older systems are always better than newer ones

questions.explanation: The house analogy explains that the main structure is designed to accommodate changes like new appliances without needing to be torn down, illustrating how original designs should consider future improvements.

questions.question: When older software struggles to run on a newer operating system, the lesson explains this issue at an 'atomic level.' What is the fundamental cause at this level?

options.A: The older software is simply too slow for modern processors
options.B: The new operating system's kernel handles low-level interactions differently, making the older software's machine code incompatible
options.C: The user forgot to install the necessary drivers for the old software
options.D: The older software was designed to be intentionally incompatible with newer systems

questions.explanation: The lesson states that at the atomic level, the issue can be linked to changes in how the new operating system's kernel handles low-level interactions, making the older software's machine code unable to execute correctly.

questions.question: A company releases a new version of its popular video game console. Users are excited to find that all their old game discs from the previous console still work perfectly on the new one. Which concept from the lesson does this scenario best demonstrate?
questions.explanation: The ability of the new console (hardware) to work with old game discs (older software/media) is a direct example of backward compatibility.

questions.question: A student is designing a robot for a science fair. They decide to build the robot's arm, body, and wheels as separate, interchangeable units, so if one part breaks or needs improvement, they can swap it out without rebuilding the whole robot. Which design principle are they applying?
questions.explanation: Designing a system with independent parts that can be easily replaced or upgraded without affecting the entire system is the definition of modularity.

questions.question: Select all the primary reasons for performing a 'System Upgrade'.

options.B: To completely replace the old system with a brand new one.
options.C: To add new features or capabilities.
options.D: To enable different systems to communicate with each other.

questions.explanation: A system upgrade is defined as a change or improvement made to a system to enhance its performance, add new features, or fix problems.

questions.question: When designing a new product, which of the following practices contribute to its long-term 'Sustainability'? (Select all that apply)

options.A: Making the initial production cost as low as possible.
options.B: Designing the system with independent parts that can be easily replaced.
options.C: Ensuring the main structure can accommodate future improvements.
options.D: Allowing new versions of the product to work with older accessories or data.

questions.explanation: Modularity (B) allows easy replacement, designing for upgrades (C) accommodates future improvements, and backward compatibility (D) extends usefulness, all contributing to a product's sustainability by ensuring it can function and serve its purpose over a long period.

questions.question: When older software struggles to run on a newer operating system, it's often because the new operating system's ___ handles low-level interactions differently, making the older software's ___ incompatible.
questions.explanation: The lesson explains that at the atomic level, the new operating system's kernel can handle low-level interactions differently, leading to incompatibility with older software's machine code.

questions.question: Imagine a company wants to create a tech product that remains useful and relevant for many years. Put these design and maintenance principles in the order they would typically be considered or applied to achieve this goal.
items: Design the system with independent, easily replaceable parts.
Ensure the product's main structure can accommodate future enhancements.
Release updates to fix problems or add new capabilities.
Enable the product to continue functioning and serving its purpose over a long period.
questions.explanation: A sustainable product (4) is achieved by designing it with modularity (1) and for future upgrades (2), which then allows for actual system upgrades (3) to be implemented over time.
